briefs.title: Atmosphere: five layers and what happens in each
briefs.intro: Draw the boundaries first, then put one process in each band. That is enough for an atmosphere question.
notes: Temperature reverses at each pause: tropopause, stratopause, mesopause.
The ozone layer sits in the stratosphere, which is why that band warms upward.

briefs.title: Glacial erosion: cirque to hanging valley
briefs.intro: One glacier produces the whole chain. Draw the cirque first, then let the ice move down-valley.
notes: Plucking and abrasion are the two processes; the landforms are what they leave behind.
A hanging valley sits above the main trough because the tributary glacier cut less deeply.

briefs.title: Volcano: chamber, conduit, crater, flow
briefs.intro: A cut-away in four labels answers both the landform and the hazard part of the question.
notes: Basaltic lava is runny and builds a shield; andesitic lava is sticky and builds a steep cone.
A caldera forms when the chamber empties and the roof collapses.

briefs.title: Mauryan administration: king to village
briefs.intro: Five rungs are enough. The answer is about control, not a list of officials.
notes: The Arthashastra and the Ashokan edicts are the two source families.
Dhamma policy sits beside the administrative machine, not instead of it.

briefs.title: Budget enactment: estimate to audit
briefs.intro: The constitutional sequence is the answer. Each step has an article you can cite.
notes: No expenditure can be incurred without parliamentary approval.
A money bill can pass in the Lok Sabha alone; the Rajya Sabha has 14 days to recommend.

briefs.title: Emergency provisions: three kinds, three triggers
briefs.intro: Put the three emergencies in one line and the federal tilt becomes obvious.
notes: National: war, external aggression or armed rebellion, on the Cabinet's written advice.
State: failure of constitutional machinery. Financial: a threat to the financial stability of India.

briefs.title: Waste hierarchy: the order is the policy
briefs.intro: Draw it as a ladder of preference, not a list. The top is what to do first.
notes: A circular-economy answer should start at the top of the ladder, not at recycling.
India's EPR rules push producers up the ladder; collection and processing are the binding constraint.

briefs.title: Eutrophication: nutrient to dead zone
briefs.intro: Five links, one causal chain. Name the nutrient and the oxygen sink.
steps:
Nutrient load
N and P runoff
notes: Agriculture runoff and untreated sewage are the two main sources in Indian lakes.
Restoration means cutting the nutrient load, not only harvesting the bloom.

briefs.title: Ethical decision-making: six steps under time pressure
briefs.intro: A GS4 case study rewards a visible method. Draw the steps, then apply them to the facts.
notes: Name the tension before you choose: that is what separates an ethical answer from a list.
The test is not only 'is it legal' but 'would I defend it in public'.
